page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a diagram (a tree of musical scales, "CLAVES") in the middle. Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 stand in the right margin. The catchword "Existi-" stands at the foot on the right.

main_text.p: obtinendum siue praeualendum in cantu, siue, adattol-lendam vocem ita vt vincantur alij. 5Eodem sensu musicis dicitur octaua, & diapason. Prius genus pleumque[?] in Chromate positum est secundo genere musices: posterius, tertio. Hac de re accipe sequentem typum.

Hoc schema est fundamentum musicae vtriusque, tum vocalis, tum instrumentalis. 304. Ad cantum rite instituendum requiruntur certi modi. Tales vulgo numerantur duodecim, e quibus sex sunt principes, puta Dorius, Phrygius, Lydius, Mixolydius, Aeolius, & Ionicus: & totidem subditi, vt puta Hypodorius, Hypophrygius, Hypolydius, Hypomixolydius, Hypoaeolius, & Hypoionicus. 35Hi modi sunt certissimus canon cantilenae cuiusque.

page.notes: The diagram's brace structure is hard to follow at this scan resolution. The outline levels are my best reading. The middle column (Diapason, Diatessaron, Diezeugmenon, Synemmenon, Meson, Hypate) and the right column (Tetrachordum V, IV, III, II, I; Symphonia acuta sive virginea; Symphonia graves; Chroma) are not transcribed as boxes. The word "pleumque" is uncertain; it may read "pleramque". The marginal numbers are printed line counters.
